description: Teach one correction after operator confirmation. From the next session on, wherever the recognizer writes the whole words in heard, the transcript says meant instead and also carries the words as recognized. A rule is blind to context: use it for a name the recognizer does not know and writes as something that is never the right word here, not for ordinary words. Matching ignores case and keeps a possessive. Teaching a heard phrase again replaces what it meant. What was meant, when it is one to four plain words, is also preferred by the recognizer itself, so a name taught once is written right more often even where it was heard as something no rule lists. At most 64 rules.

heard.description: One to four words exactly as the recognizer writes them, separated by single spaces: letters, digits and apostrophes only, no punctuation.

meant.description: What those words meant, written as it should appear. One line, no leading or trailing space, different from heard.

revision.description: Exact revision returned by vocabulary.list; a stale revision refuses without changing the list.
